newsitem.title: USA: Mass. pulls counsel for insurance dept.-report.
newsitem.headline: Mass. pulls counsel for insurance dept.-report.

text.p: The Massachusetts Attorney General's office has decided to no longer represent the state commissioner of insurance in a fight with a consumer group related to a stock offering, the Boston Globe reported Wednesday.
The split is likely to add to criticism of Massachusetts insurance division head Linda Ruthardt, the newspaper said.

The attorney general's office, which is in charge of representing state agencies in court, said it is pulling out because "the division provided us with inaccurate information," the newspaper reported.
According to letters obtained by the Globe, the attorney general's office had "serious concern" about "ethical issues" raised by the division's conduct.

The split grows out of hearings on the demutualization of State Mutual Life Assurance Co of Worcester, Mass., which touched off a battle between the insurance division and a consumer group, the Center for Insurance Research in Cambridge. The center believes that the insurance division has withheld documents on negotiations between the state and the company, the Globe said.
The parties did not return calls seeking comments.
